summary_html: Court issues a **protective or restraining order** to prevent contact, remove abuser, or ensure safety without removing the child. Federal law leaves implementation to states but funds protection efforts through CAPTA and IV-B.
authority_html:
- **CAPTA (42 U.S.C. §§ 5101–5116)** — authorizes protective interventions and state plan requirements  
- **SSA Title IV-B** — permits funding for protective services and court interventions

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that KRS 403.750 permits a trial court to extend a domestic violence order's protection to the petitioner's minor child on a preponderance showing that domestic violence occurred and may again occur, but that where the child is also the respondent's child the court must apply KRS 403.320(2); it reversed in part for an evidentiary error at the amendment hearing.
key_cases.relevance: This is the Kentucky authority on extending or amending a domestic violence order to protect a child without removing the child from the home.
key_cases.quote: The preponderance of the evidence standard is met when the evidence establishes that the petitioner "was more likely than not to have been a victim of domestic violence."

key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
key_cases.holding: In a case against Kentucky CHFS social workers, the court held the Fourth Amendment governs a social worker's warrantless in-school interview of a child and requires at least reasonable suspicion of abuse (though that right was not clearly established, so those defendants received qualified immunity), and it affirmed the denial of qualified immunity on the parents' substantive and procedural due-process claims arising from a coerced 'prevention plan' that restricted a mother's unsupervised contact with her children.
key_cases.relevance: The supervision restrictions imposed by the prevention plan functioned as a de facto protective order and were held to implicate the family-integrity right.
key_cases.quote: a social worker must have a reasonable suspicion of child abuse before conducting an in-school interview when no other exception to the Fourth Amendment's warrant requirement applies

key_cases.case_name: A.P. v. Commonwealth, Cabinet for Health & Family Services
key_cases.holding: The court vacated a termination judgment because the family court conducted the first day of the termination trial, taking two witnesses' testimony, while the mother's appointed counsel was absent, holding that the mother was denied the due process to which she was entitled and ordering a new hearing with counsel present throughout.
key_cases.relevance: The no-contact condition of the safety plan functioned as a protective arrangement short of removal.
key_cases.quote: Kentucky's statutory scheme to protect children and to adjudicate parental rights provides for the appointment of counsel throughout all the proceedings
